title: Locally built plugins group source and sink connectors

nodes.summary: Taps are Git catalogues distributing plugin, library and template packages
nodes.detail: A tap is a Git repository with a data catalogue distributing three package kinds (plugins, reusable MicroHs libraries, KB templates); any third-party tap or local checkout works without a central approval service, and first-party packages use the same interfaces.

realised.evidence: No tap, library-package or template-package code existed before the tap model was redefined at seq 114

nodes.summary: Plugins ship as source, vendored into the KB and compiled locally
nodes.detail: Distributed plugins are inspectable source directories, vendored with their source dependencies into the KB's Git tree and compiled locally against the installed SDK/runtime; no supplied executables, and compiled artifacts are disposable build products.

realised.evidence: Vendoring lands with PR #89/#90 (seq 73-74); PR #100 compiles vendored local-file source and hashes captured source for package identity. Source-dependency vendoring itself is still not implemented (packages are self-contained)

nodes.summary: Evidence methods supply citable source identifiers, no version obligation
nodes.detail: Evidence-producing methods should supply a stable URI, scoped provider item ID or local path so citations stay meaningful outside Kyyn's evidence cache; no source-version, fingerprint or historical-reconstruction obligation attaches to citations.

realised.evidence: Local-file evidence is keyed by file path once configured fetches land (PR #101); Graph events later carry provider IDs

nodes.summary: One plugin supplies connector types; KB configures named instances
nodes.detail: A plugin supplies connector types (config type, implementation, methods), each a Source or Sink; the KB configures uniquely named instances beneath the plugin, repeated types allowed, referenced by plugin plus instance name. No kernel Connection entity or per-instance install lifecycle.

realised.evidence: PR #100 registers source connectors with root-owned Dhall instance configuration and proves two independent Folder instances; sink connector types are still not implemented

nodes.summary: Single typed method registration and checked host invocation boundary
nodes.detail: Fixed health/description/config methods and typed named methods share one registration mechanism; the host listMethods/callPlugin boundary checks input and output contracts against structural descriptors, with no unchecked byte-call escape hatch.

realised.evidence: The generic listMethods/callPlugin host API never appeared in code; the prepared-plugin/PluginRead boundary that replaced it at seq 143 is what was built

nodes.summary: Invocations select plugin and instance; config is typed input
nodes.detail: A connector call names plugin and connector instance rather than an ambient default account; the selected instance's concrete configuration is assembled into the method's typed input by generated bindings, and dispatch verifies the method belongs to that connector type.

realised.evidence: PR #101 exposes configured per-instance fetching through the CLI; PR #107 adds per-instance handles for KB tools

nodes.summary: Explicit plugin update re-fetches source from recorded origin
nodes.detail: A dedicated update operation (e.g. `kyyn plugin update`) fetches from the recorded remote origin, re-vendors and rebuilds the whole plugin package, preserving configuration/credentials and refusing to silently overwrite local source edits.

realised.evidence: No separate update command was built; re-installation became the update route at seq 120

nodes.summary: No plugin version pins, compatibility declarations or solver
nodes.detail: First release deliberately has no version pins, SDK/runtime compatibility declarations, negotiation or backward-compatibility promise; incompatible updates are repaired via compiler diagnostics and Git, and old compiled artifacts are never selected for changed source.

realised.evidence: Negative constraint; no version machinery existed at founding and none was added

nodes.summary: Install/update stage local files adopted through ordinary evolution
nodes.detail: Installation and update prepare local files only; they never create a special install commit or silently accept a new root, so changes are adopted through the ordinary code-only evolution route or Git with checking on load.

realised.evidence: PR #89 installs into the KB without commits, HEAD changes or acceptance

nodes.summary: Trust selected source and toolchain; no signing or attestation
nodes.detail: Building the source it executes removes executable-provenance concerns; Kyyn introduces no plugin signing, provenance attestations, reproducible-build gates or central trust service. Review is ordinary judgement, not a runtime gate.
sections: Decision / Trust the selected source and the installed toolchain

realised.evidence: Negative constraint; no signing or trust machinery exists

nodes.summary: Install from local directory or Git URL subdirectory with origin
nodes.detail: `plugin install --from DIR|URL [--path SUB]` captures a package copy (local working-tree contents or fetched Git HEAD) into root/plugins/packages/<name>/source with Kyyn-owned origin.dhall recording source and path, excluding .git/build directories and refusing symlinks, submodules and existing destinations.

realised.evidence: PR #87 implementing this was paused; the local working-tree route was replaced by Git-only acquisition before shipping

nodes.summary: Hermetic kyyn-plugin.dhall manifest names package and entry module
nodes.detail: The package root is the directory containing a hermetic kyyn-plugin.dhall `{ name, entryModule }`; the entry module must exist under src/. The manifest locates source only; method and config schemas stay in Haskell declarations.

realised.evidence: PR #87 adds PluginManifest and decoding; plugins/local-file manifest ships in PR #90

nodes.summary: Installation validates structure only, with no runtime or commit effects
nodes.detail: Installation validates package structure without guest compilation, configuration, health or evidence; it creates no commit, changes no accepted HEAD and accepts nothing, leaving an ordinary local root change for the owner to adopt. Stable plugin.* refusal codes.

realised.evidence: PR #89 runtime-free PluginInstallation porcelain with structured refusals

nodes.summary: Install only committed Git revisions; origin records revision
nodes.detail: Every source is a Git repository: local packages are read from committed HEAD, dirty package paths are refused (plugin.source-uncommitted), and origin.dhall records repository, repository-relative path and exact captured revision. The filesystem tree-reader route is dropped.

realised.evidence: PR #87 (seq 72) adds Git-backed acquisition and revision-bearing PluginOrigin; PR #89 (seq 73) installs; PR #90 (seq 74) CLI

nodes.summary: Each connector instance declares its generated guest binding name
nodes.detail: Root-owned instances carry a BindingName for their generated guest binding under ADR 0016; the binding is an authoring name, not another identity, so renaming it does not rename the instance or its history.

realised.evidence: BindingName and global binding checks land in PR #100; executable bindings in PR #107

nodes.summary: Plugin-specific captured-evidence read methods, no generic evidence view
nodes.detail: Sources expose plugin-specific typed methods over captured evidence (e.g. viewEmail) that are separately discoverable and composable in KB tools; the host prescribes no generic evidence view, and acquisition and captured reads have distinct capability rows.

realised.evidence: PR #106 adds local-file content method discovery and invocation over latest evidence

nodes.summary: Plugin installation targets an unaccepted evolution only
nodes.detail: `plugin install --evolution ID` writes into evolutions/<id>/target/plugins/packages; missing or accepted evolutions are refused before acquisition, changing a target stales prior checks, and the accepted root changes only on acceptance. No direct-to-root mode for install, update or removal.

realised.evidence: PR #98 implements target-scoped installation with installed install/check/accept journeys

nodes.summary: Connectors registered via entry module's SourceConnector list with named types
nodes.detail: A plugin entry module exports `connectors :: [SourceConnector]` naming connector, config/payload types, fetch and pure validateConfig by qualified Haskell names; the compiler inspects named types and generated adapters typecheck the functions, deriving a Dhall config union without duplicated schemas.

realised.evidence: PR #100 implements registration, inspection, generated adapters and root-wide config validation

nodes.summary: CapturedMethod declarations and PluginRead invoke typed captured reads
nodes.detail: Connector declarations list CapturedMethod entries (name, description, implementation); generated adapters check them against CapturedRead, and the PluginRead capability validates input, loads current evidence once and calls the read with no file-acquisition capability or live fallback.

realised.evidence: PR #106 implements CapturedMethod registration, PluginRead and CLI method list/show/execute

nodes.summary: Optional typed fetch options checked before acquisition
nodes.detail: A connector may advertise an options type; its contract is discoverable via `plugin connector show`, supplied options are checked before guest execution, and the fetch signature takes `Maybe Options` while no-options connectors keep their existing signature.

realised.evidence: PR #145 implements fetchOptionsType, checked --options and history retention

nodes.summary: Connectors declare FileSource or NetworkSource acquisition context
nodes.detail: Each source connector selects an acquisition context that picks ADR 0009's file/evidence row or HTTP/secret/evidence row, determining generated signatures and native dispatch.

realised.evidence: Never implemented; dropped in favour of one unified acquisition row when Graph shipped (seq 113)

nodes.summary: Optional connector login entry dispatched under ADR 0016
nodes.detail: A source connector may name a login entry checked and dispatched under ADR 0016's plugin-owned authentication; discovery shows the declaration without executing authentication or fetching.

realised.evidence: PR #147 adds CLI connector login and Graph device-code/client-secret auth

nodes.summary: All source connectors share one acquisition capability row
nodes.detail: Every source connector uses ADR 0009's single acquisition row (files, HTTP, secrets, waiting, evidence reads); login presence is independent of which capabilities a fetch uses.

realised.evidence: PR #147 unifies the acquisition row and dispatcher and ships the Graph calendar source

nodes.summary: KB-local taps.dhall declares taps; synced catalogues are disposable caches
nodes.detail: A KB's tracked top-level taps.dhall (outside root/evolution ownership) names tap repositories; synced catalogues live in ignored .kyyn/taps; search is offline; `tap/plugin` names resolve through the existing installer and execution never resolves a tap. No global registry; tap updates never change installed plugins.
sections: Decision / Discover packages through KB-local taps

realised.evidence: PR #155 implements taps.dhall, tap list/add/remove/update, search and qualified install

nodes.summary: Package README is the guide, read host-side without executing plugins
nodes.detail: A plugin's guide is its package-root README.md; the host reads it for installed, evolution or not-yet-installed (tap) packages without compiling, authenticating or validating the root.
sections: Decision / Read packaged guides without executing plugins

realised.evidence: PR #154 (seq 118) reads installed guides; PR #155 (seq 119) adds pre-installation guide access

nodes.summary: Registration names functions; contracts derived from checked signatures
nodes.detail: Connector and method registration names implementations only; the compiler derives Config, Payload, optional Options and captured-method Input/Result from checked function signatures, rejecting misfits, using payload-parameterised SDK types instead of a generated KyynPluginBindings module.

realised.evidence: PR #151 implements signature-derived preparation and migrates first-party plugins

nodes.summary: Repeat install replaces the package and is the update route
nodes.detail: Re-running `plugin install` in an evolution replaces the named package completely (removing obsolete files, updating origin, preserving connector config); this replaces both the duplicate-install refusal and any separate update command or force flag.

realised.evidence: PR #156 implements staged complete re-vendoring with rollback

nodes.summary: Evolution review shows host-derived plugin package comparisons
nodes.detail: Evolution check/show reports added, removed and changed plugin packages with before/after origin and changed paths from package bytes (so local edits under an unchanged origin show), persisted with candidate and accepted reports.

realised.evidence: PR #157 persists plugin comparisons in EvolutionRecord v4 and renders them

nodes.summary: Host plugin boundary is preparation plus typed captured-read execution
nodes.detail: Host contracts are PluginPreparation (prepare packages/plugins, validate configs without provider calls) yielding PreparedConnector/PreparedMethod, and PluginRead (LoadCapturedInput, ExecuteCapturedMethod) with checked contracts; sinks are owned by ADR 0017, replacing the generic callPlugin API.

realised.evidence: PreparePackages/PreparedPackage existed from seq 82 and LoadCapturedInput/ExecuteCapturedMethod from seq 87; the reconciliation adopted them as contract

nodes.summary: Typed connector sync positions derived from fetch signatures
nodes.detail: Stateful fetch signatures take FetchContext Position and return FetchResult Payload Position; Position is derived from the checked signature like Config/Payload/Options and kept through PreparedConnector and generated dispatch.

realised.evidence: PR #203 infers FetchContext/FetchResult from signatures and persists positions

nodes.summary: One microsoft-graph package holds Calendar, Mail, Meetings, Files sources
nodes.detail: A single microsoft-graph plugin supplies Calendar, Mail, Meetings and Files source types with per-instance config, evidence and sync position, sharing plugin auth code; Mail/Meetings/Files expose typed captured reads and BlobRefs rather than eager binary content.

realised.evidence: plugins/microsoft-graph in kyyn-v2 only contains the Calendar source (Calendar.hs); no Mail, Meetings or Files connectors yet

editorial.note: Only adds retained Git refusal codes to the diagnostics list; the PR delivers the CLI that realises the install nodes
Rewords citation guidance to point operational fingerprints at ADR 0014; citations still need no version or fingerprint
Status wording only: marks fetch options as implemented (realises 0015.20)
Removes the 'not yet implemented' status line for signature-derived registration (realises 0015.26)
Status wording only: installed-package list/show/guide implemented
Status wording and naming the repository-root kyyn-tap.dhall catalogue file; realises tap discovery and pre-install guides

notes: The founding text is ambitious (taps with library/template packages, sinks, a generic callPlugin host API, a dedicated update command), and most of it was either narrowed or replaced by what got built: tap kinds collapsed to plugin-only catalogues (seq 114), callPlugin became PluginPreparation/PluginRead (reconciled at seq 143, code-first), and `plugin update` became repeat install (seq 120). The install slice flip-flopped quickly: seq 70 specified installing local working-tree contents, then seq 71 (same day, before implementation shipped) made it Git-only with revision-bearing origins; seq 79 then moved the install target from root/ into an evolution. Registration went through two shapes: named type strings (seq 81) then signature-derived contracts (seq 115/116), absorbing the short-lived fetchOptionsType field; AcquisitionContext (seq 110) never shipped and was replaced by a unified row at seq 113. Spec ahead of code at end of history: sink connectors, source-dependency vendoring, and the Graph Mail/Meetings/Files family (seq 151) remain unrealised. Split judgement: the founding 'One plugin, several connectors' subsection was split into hierarchy (04), typed method boundary (05) and instance-selected dispatch (06); 'Explicit updates' was split into the update operation (07), the no-versioning constraint (08) and evolution adoption (09). Seq 143 also removed the ConnectorKind Source|Sink type from the code block while keeping kind as 'intended use' text; treated as editorial within 0015.29.
